tob-0152: The Vision and the Voice logs Crowley’s scryings of the thirty Enochian Aethyrs in the Algerian waste in 1909 — sights of angels, devils, and world-vistas, spoken to his scribe. It is his most singing and most dread work. The book crowns his wonder-working life.
tob-13152: A. E. Waite’s Holy Grail is the great sifting of the Grail tale — its Keltic roots, Christian shapes, and hidden senses. The scholar-wise man’s huge work stays the last word on the theme. The book is needful for Grail seekers.
cia-0000107452: Observations on Palestine and the Arab countries, dated February 1949 — months after Israel's founding war. The Middle East was being redrawn by armistice lines and refugee camps, and American observers were taking its measure. The document preserves first impressions of a conflict that would define the region for generations.
cia-0000112352: A March 1988 report on Chinese scientists identifying a Xinjiang UFO as a plasma fireball — a natural electrical phenomenon. Here was the sober counterpart to saucer fever: experts explaining the lights away. The document shows science doing its job, with the CIA taking notes.
cia-0000112752: A March 1984 study — part of its title deleted — on South Africa's turn to heavy water technology and what it meant. Heavy water can help make plutonium for bombs, so Pretoria's interest was alarming. The document tracks the technical trail of a secret weapons program, one reactor choice at a time.
cia-0000117852: A July 1969 FBIS trends piece on Vietnam, introducing the Paris peace talks. The Foreign Broadcast Information Service turned communist media into intelligence, and its trend pieces spotted the direction of the wind. The entry shows analysts reading Hanoi's newspapers for hints of flexibility at the negotiating table.
cia-0000115452: A January 1980 interagency memo on the growth and prospects of leftist extremists in El Salvador. The guerrilla movement was gaining ground, and Washington debated how red the threat really was. The memo captures the intelligence community's early read on a war that would kill tens of thousands.
cia-0000118652: A January 1980 report on Soviet preparations for the Olympic Games in Moscow. The USSR was staging its coming-out party — new stadiums, showcase projects, and a charm offensive. The CIA watched the preparations the way it watched everything Soviet: for what the spectacle revealed about the system behind it.
cia-0000119752: The Hungarian situation as of 5:00 PM on November 7, 1956 — three days after the Soviet invasion, with organized resistance crushed. Budapest was under occupation; the new Soviet-backed regime was taking hold. The document records the aftermath: a revolution ended, a crackdown begun.
cia-0000132752: A 1961 report titled Cuba and the Carribbean — the archive's spelling doubles the r. The basin, surveyed. The document is the neighborhood: the islands, assessed.
cia-0000134252: Item 12 in a 1960 series: the Venezuelan and Peruvian foreign ministers possibly resigning over an OAS meeting — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The Cuba debate was toppling ministers. The document is the fallout: the resignations, rumored.
cia-0000135952: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting a list of compromised cryptonyms and pseudonyms — the truncated title suggests more. Blown code names were dangerous. The document is the damage control: the names, listed — the burned, identified.
cia-0000136052: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting current information on the sixth military zone at Quiche. The Guatemalan highlands, mapped militarily. The document is the zone: the region, assessed.
cia-0000136352: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK on a meeting being broken up due to unacceptable something — the truncated title cuts off the noun. The talks collapsed. The document is the breakup: the meeting, ended.
cia-0000136952: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN requesting the completest dateline coverage of local press — the truncated title cuts off the rest. The newspapers, fully watched. The document is the coverage: the press, complete.
un-ga-res-1952: Resolution 1952 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1963. The early-sixties Assembly at work. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-ga-res-1752: Resolution 1752 of the General Assembly, adopted in 1962. The Cuban missile crisis year's Assembly. The number and year are preserved; the decision lives in the text.
un-ga-res-a-69-52: Resolution A/69/52, cataloged with the year 2004 — the mismatch again. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-52: Security Council Resolution 52, adopted in 1948. The early Council deciding. The number and year endure; the decision belongs to the text.
un-sc-res-452: Security Council Resolution 452, adopted in July 1979 — the settlements resolution, declaring Israeli settlements in the occupied territories illegal and an obstacle to peace. The Council's legal verdict on the settlement enterprise. The resolution is the ruling: the settlements, unlawful.
un-sc-res-652: Security Council Resolution 652, adopted in 1990 — aligned. The Gulf crisis year's Council. The designation and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1552: Security Council Resolution 1552, cataloged with the year 2005 — the numbering suggests 2004, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1952: Security Council Resolution 1952, adopted in 2010 — aligned. The deliberations rolled on. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
cia-0000132652: A 1961 CIA study of probable international reactions to certain possible US courses of action — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Washington gamed the world's response to its Cuba options. The document is the gaming: the reactions, predicted.
cia-0000136552: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136552. The training year's papers, a later archive number. The document is the training: the papers, early.
plos-pone-0000052: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper on the impact of neuroprotection on the incidence of Alzheimer's disease. Could protecting neurons prevent Alzheimer's? The paper is the impact: the protection, weighed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d52: Prime Minister Churchill to President Roosevelt, October 22, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 52. The next day, the answer. The message is the answer: the prime minister, prompt.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d152: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 21, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 152. Washington to London. The message is the link: the allies, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d252: A memorandum by the ambassador to the Soviet Union, Harriman, November 23 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 252. Moscow's envoy, on paper. The memo is the envoy's: Harriman, recording.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d352: The president's secretary Early to the president's special assistant — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 352. The staff wrote back. The memo is the volley: Early, again.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d452: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 452. The editors' hinge. The note is the hinge: the documents, swinging.
arxiv-2605-09052: Enceladus, Saturn's icy moon, sprays geysers from a hidden ocean — but how deep does the water go? This 2026 paper probes the moon's interior with electromagnetic induction, reading how Saturn's magnetic field soaks into the ice to map the ocean below. It is planetary science without a drill.
arxiv-2605-09152: Understanding cats — their postures, vocalizations, moods — is feline ethology, and now it gets a multimodal AI. Jucheng Hu presents Meow-Omni 1, a multimodal large language model for studying cat behavior. The 2026 paper is delightfully serious: AI-assisted animal behavior science.
arxiv-2605-09352: Do vision, sound, and touch all converge on language as their shared representation — as Wittgenstein might have predicted? Zhaoyang Zhang, Run Shao, Dongyue Wu, and colleagues put the Wittgensteinian representation hypothesis to the test. The 2026 paper is philosophy-tinged AI science at its most provocative and fun.
arxiv-2605-09652: Constrained optimization algorithms stall — and a well-timed stagnation kick can restart them. Dikshant, Dikshit Chauhan, Chen Hao, and colleagues add Cauchy mutation, an archive, and a stagnation kick to RDEx for constrained problems. The 2026 paper is evolutionary optimization with restart tricks.
arxiv-2605-09752: Quantum-mechanics/molecular-mechanics splits a system into a quantum core and a classical surroundings; polarizable embedding lets the surroundings respond to the core. Julian Beßner, Anoop A. K. Nair, Magnus A. H. Christiansen, and colleagues extend the approach to periodic systems. The 2026 paper is computational chemistry for crystals and materials.
arxiv-2605-09852: Explanations of AI decisions should themselves be fair — a unifying framework with axioms and future directions. Gideon Popoola and John Sheppard build that framework from the ground up. The 2026 paper demands fairness for explanations, not just for the predictions themselves.
arxiv-2605-10052: Swarm skills — portable, self-evolving specifications for multi-agent coordination engineering. The openJiuwen Team and Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence develop the specification. The 2026 paper is multi-agent systems with skills that travel and evolve. It engineers coordination that evolves.
plos-pone-0003452: Cancer researchers fished a drug clue out of a patient's blood in this 2008 paper. Screening antibody fragments from a cancer patient, they isolated a peptide that latches onto human interleukin-11, a cytokine already FDA-approved for low platelet counts. The peptide marks the receptor-interacting site, a foothold for designing drugs that tune IL-11's effects in cancer.
plos-pone-0003552: Communication researchers showed headlines reshape how we fear disease in this 2008 study. As pandemic talk fills the popular press, media coverage shifted people's perceptions of disease risk, often out of proportion to the actual threat. The findings reveal the media's power to set the public's sense of danger.
plos-pone-0003652: In 2008, a team read tiny RNAs in prion disease. As prions wrecked the brain, the levels of these small gene-tuners shifted in a set pattern. That RNA pattern marks the brain damage as it unfolds, giving clues to how brain cells fail.
plos-pone-0003752: In 2008, Caiado, Real, and Carvalho tuned vessel-building with a cell signal. Adjusting Notch signaling in bone-marrow-derived vascular precursors changed their ability to grow new blood vessels and heal wounds. The dial offers control over the body's own repair crew.
plos-pone-0003852: Back in 2008, a group cleared a diabetes suspect. Their meta-analysis found no link between the SOCS3 gene's A+930G variant and type 2 diabetes. The negative result closes the case on one candidate, letting diabetes genetics focus its search elsewhere.
plos-pone-0003952: In 2008, Linden, Florin, and McGuckin watched gut mucus during bacterial attack. Mucin dynamics in Citrobacter rodentium infection of mice modeled human bacterial gastroenteritis. The study reveals the mucus layer as an active defender, not passive slime.
plos-pone-0004052: In 2008, Habig, Aruscavage, and Bass found a shortcut around a missing helper. High doses of double-stranded RNA triggered gene silencing without the RDE-4 helper. RDE-4 normally helps the Dicer enzyme start RNA interference in worms. The bypass reveals RNAi's backup routes when the usual guide is gone.
plos-pone-0004152: In 2009, Chakraborty, Uechi, and Higa broke a ribosome piece in fish embryos. Losing ribosomal protein L11 derailed young zebrafish embryo development. The p53-driven cell-death response badly overreacted to the loss. The fish model illuminates ribosome-related human birth defects.
plos-pone-0004252: In 2009, Farke, Wolff, and Tanke found horned dinosaurs dueling. Skull lesions on Triceratops pointed to combat between horned dinosaurs clearly. The horns and frill served as weapons, not just for display. The fossil wounds rewrite ceratopsian social life for good.
plos-pone-0004352: In 2009, Hagan, O'Neill, and Stewart mapped a parent-stamped gene block. At least ten genes defined the imprinted Dlk1-Dio3 cluster on mouse chromosome 12. The genes obeyed parental origin. The map aids imprinting research. The cluster is a hotspot for imprinting disorders.
plos-pone-0358752: Swine fever outbreaks demand fast temperature checks on pigs, and a color-changing earplug could do it passively. This paper tested how coating composition and thickness affect thermochromic performance — the sharpness of the color change with temperature. The work tunes the materials so the earplug’s color reliably signals a fever.
plos-pone-0358652: University life can break as well as build minds. This national survey mapped risk and protective factors for mental health in Indonesian academia. The findings show what drives distress among students and staff — and what buffers it — giving universities a blueprint for support.
plos-pone-0358452: Patients with delusional parasitosis are convinced parasites infest their skin — though none exist. This paper bridged perception and reality by examining what such patients submit as ‘parasites’ for laboratory identification. The findings help dermatologists and psychiatrists respond with both scientific clarity and human compassion.
plos-pone-0358352: HIV drugs only suppress the virus if patients take them faithfully, every day. This systematic review and meta-analysis measured the effect of antiretroviral therapy adherence on viral load suppression among people living with HIV in Ethiopia. The pooled evidence quantifies adherence’s payoff in hard numbers for program planners.
plos-pone-0357952: Nitric oxide is a crucial signal in muscle — but measuring it reliably in tissue is notoriously tricky. This paper tested the reliability of biochemical assays of nitric oxide biomarkers in human skeletal muscle samples. The validation tells researchers exactly which measurements they can trust and which ones mislead.
plos-pone-0349852: After hand injury, relative motion orthoses guide healing — but what do the patients wearing them actually think? This scoping review protocol will gather patient-perspective evidence on the acceptability, usability, and everyday impact of these devices in adult hand rehabilitation. The planned review puts the wearer’s voice first.
plos-pone-0357752: Tiny aborted RNA fragments floating in exosomes might flag Alzheimer’s years before symptoms. This paper explored abortive transcripts in exosomes as a potential biomarker for Alzheimer’s disease. The blood-based signal could one day enable earlier diagnosis, when interventions have the best chance to help.
plos-pone-0355752: Fragmented insurance-based health systems routinely fail patients with multiple chronic conditions. This Colombian mixed-methods study designed a provider-led multimorbidity care model built for exactly such fragmented systems. The model offers a practical blueprint where single-disease care keeps falling short.
plos-pone-0357452: Intermediate wheatgrass could become humanity’s first perennial grain crop. This paper assessed genomic prediction accuracy and expected genetic gain in multi-population half-sib families of the grass. The genetics work accelerates breeding toward a wheat that never needs replanting.
plos-pone-0343652: How the media frames a farming technology shapes whether farmers adopt it. This paper analyzed media framing of agricultural technology adoption in developing countries through Juncao technology news coverage. The framing patterns show which narratives help — and which quietly sabotage — new agricultural ideas.
plos-pone-0350952: Elite female footballers’ leg strength, side-to-side asymmetry, and jumping power were measured in this cross-sectional study. The data on lower limb muscle strength, inter-limb asymmetry, and vertical jump performance give coaches evidence-based benchmarks for training and injury prevention.
plos-pone-0353852: After traumatic brain injury, the brain’s waste-clearance system — the glymphatic system — falters. This paper showed propranolol, a common beta-blocker, improves cognitive function and glymphatic recovery through the STAT3/MMP2 pathway after TBI. Repurposing this cheap, familiar drug could transform brain injury care.
plos-pone-0353352: Atherosclerosis — artery-clogging plaque — involves cellular self-eating gone wrong. This paper identified CASP1 as a key autophagy-related gene in atherosclerosis through bioinformatics analysis plus experimental validation. The validated target offers a new foothold against the world’s leading killer.
plos-pone-0355952: Autonomic dysfunction — when the nervous system’s autopilot fails — produces bewildering, invisible suffering. This paper gathered the lived experiences and perspectives of persons with these conditions. Their voices demand that medicine take seriously what it cannot easily measure.
plos-pone-0356052: When a patient dies by suicide, the psychiatrist carries the weight. This paper examined the experience and impact of patient suicide on psychiatrists in Malaysia. The candid accounts break professional silence around a trauma the medical culture expects doctors to absorb alone.
plos-pone-0355852: Antihistamines — among the world’s most used drugs — cause adverse reactions worth characterizing. This descriptive analysis drew on WHO-VigiAccess data for two antihistamine drugs. The global pharmacovigilance picture reveals side effect patterns that individual countries’ data can’t show alone.
plos-pone-0339752: Video consultations change the nurse–patient relationship — Danish cardiac nurses have views. This qualitative focus group study explored their perspectives. The nurses’ insights reveal what’s gained and lost when care goes virtual — essential as telehealth becomes permanent.
plos-pone-0354952: Genes load the dice for high blood pressure — including the kind clinics miss. This Liechtenstein population study linked genetic predisposition to high blood pressure and out-of-office hypertension. The findings show DNA shapes the hypertension that white-coat measurements never catch.
plos-pone-0355552: Geographic atrophy — blinding macular degeneration — might yield to neural stem cells. This paper presented an improved formulation of human neural stem cells for its treatment. The refined cell therapy inches toward restoring vision that medicine currently cannot save.
europmc-pmc2798952: Asthma has long been blamed on allergies and airways alone, but this 2010 paper looks at the microbes living in asthmatic lungs. The authors find the bacterial communities in patients' airways are disordered compared with healthy people. The discovery suggests disturbed lung microbes may contribute to asthma. It opened a new front in understanding and treating the disease.
europmc-pmc2809052: A swollen heart muscle flags harm, and MRI can spot the swell. This 2009 paper sharpens that scan with T2 gauging, which reads a magnetic trait of flesh with care. The team shows it finds heart swell more surely than old ways. Faster spotting aids quick care for heart ills.
europmc-pmc2825552: Sudden kidney injury involves a storm of inflammatory signals. This 2009 review surveys the mediators of inflammation in acute kidney injury. The authors organize what drives the damaging immune response. Understanding these mediators matters because blocking the right ones could protect kidneys. The review gathered a scattered literature into one place.
europmc-pmc2848652: Front-line care wears many masks round the globe. This 2010 review charts what front-line care means, naming its core facets. The authors fuse what the trade agrees on. Their frame gave plan chiefs one tongue for firming first-contact care.
europmc-pmc2958552: West Nile virus hit American birds hard in 1999, and this 2003 paper tests why. The authors experimentally infect North American birds with the New York 1999 strain. Their work reveals avian vulnerability. The study guided surveillance. Crows died fastest, the tests showed.
europmc-pmc2996852: Rice senses fungal attack with paired receptors. This 2010 paper shows two chitin-sensing proteins, CEBiP and OsCERK1, team up to sound the alarm in rice. The authors reveal the teamwork. Their work aids disease-proof crops. Breeders now stack these sensors in new strains.
europmc-pmc3012052: Edible insects may beat cattle on emissions. This 2010 paper measures greenhouse gas and ammonia from food-grade insect species. The authors' numbers favor bugs over beef. Their work backs insect protein. Crickets puff a fraction of cow methane. Climate menus may soon feature mealworms.
europmc-pmc3029252: Bacteria grow gene families by swapping, not copying. This 2011 paper shows germs trade genes sideways to build big protein families. The authors reveal the swapping habit. Their work reframed germ evolution. Antibiotic resistance rides these swaps. The finding rewrote microbiology textbooks.
europmc-pmc3072352: Autistic kids' gut germs got compared. This 2011 paper compares gut germs and gut health in autistic versus typical kids. The authors find real differences. Their work fueled gut-brain research. Tougher autism tracked with worse gut trouble. Probiotic trials followed the findings.
europmc-pmc6520952: Children do not choose their cravings in a vacuum - food marketing shapes them. This systematic critical review finds that ads for unhealthy foods shift kids' attitudes, preferences, and actual eating toward junk. The authors detail the persuasive tricks involved, from cartoon characters to advergames, and argue the evidence supports tighter rules on marketing aimed at children.
europmc-pmc6523452: Modern biology measures genes, proteins, and metabolites by the thousands, but combining those data layers remains hard. This paper collects viewpoints from the metabolomics community on stitching multi-omics data into systems-level understanding. The authors argue that only by integrating the layers can researchers see the full circuitry of cells - and they map the practical and statistical hurdles in the way.
europmc-pmc6593152: Dirty water and poor sanitation still sicken and kill millions - through diarrhea, pneumonia, worms, and more. This updated analysis tallies the global disease burden from unsafe water, sanitation, and hygiene, disease by disease. The numbers show where clean-water investments would save the most lives.
europmc-pmc6606852: Tuberculosis bacteria are masters of hide-and-seek inside human cells. This review follows Mycobacterium tuberculosis through space and time: how it enters macrophages, dodges killing, and builds a long-term home. Understanding the choreography of infection reveals where new drugs and vaccines might strike.
europmc-pmc6667152: Once dismissed as cellular trash, extracellular vesicles are now star messengers. This review tours what is known - and unknown - about these membrane bubbles: what they carry, how they form, and what they do. The 'known unknowns' framing maps a young field's biggest open questions.
europmc-pmc6683152: Depression after 60 tangles with failing health - each feeding the other in a vicious loop. This review unpacks late-life depression's biology, from shortened telomeres to inflamed brains, and what treatments work best. Untangling the knot demands treating mind and body together.
europmc-pmc6711452: Your brain has an age - and it may not match your birthday. Brain age delta is the gap between the age a scan suggests and the years you have actually lived. This paper shows how to estimate it from brain imaging and why the delta matters: an older-looking brain can flag hidden decline.
europmc-pmc6721852: Mesenchymal stem cells - harvestable from bone marrow, fat, and joint lining - are regenerative medicine's workhorses. This review surveys their uses: rebuilding tissue, calming immune overreactions, and the practical hurdles. The versatile cells keep inching from promise toward clinic.
europmc-pmc6754952: Stem cell transplants heal skin wounds - but the cells' tiny parcels may do the job alone. This study shows MSC-derived exosomes push macrophages toward the healing M2 state, speeding cutaneous wound closure. The cell-free treatment captures the benefit without the baggage of live cells.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-52: GAO told the Air Force in 2007 to write real rules for buying and running its business software. The service was spending big on finance and supply programs with no firm playbook for picking winners. The report targets a classic Pentagon trap: billion-dollar tech buys launched on hope, then nursed along long past the point of no return.
gao-gaoreports-b-309752: A mega-ruling from GAO in 2007: seven case numbers, two firms — Contingency Management Group and IAP Worldwide Services — all fighting over rapid-response federal deals. The combined call sorts each firm's gripes under one roof. Its sheer size mirrors the prize: the big, fast-moving contracts that feed off overseas operations.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-752: Your Social Security number was public property in 2007 — GAO's report says federal moves could shrink its exposure in public records, though other leaks stayed open. The findings map the identity battlefield. The report argues for plugging the government's own holes first.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-652: Bird flu was circling in 2007 — GAO's report says the farm agency had taken real steps to ready for outbreaks, but sharper planning would speed the response. The findings credit the prep and prod the plans. The report treats the next poultry plague as a matter of when.
gao-gaoreports-b-299452: Rothe Computer Solutions, doing business as Rohmann Joint Venture, took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the call. The venture challenged the award; the ruling tests the claims. Joint ventures get joint answers in bid court.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-352: Reagan National's runways were maxed out in 2007, and GAO's report updates the airport's capacity and the ripple effects on its neighbors. The findings map the squeeze. The report asks how many more planes the little airport on the river could take.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-152: Leaking gas station tanks were poisoning groundwater in 2007, and GAO's report says the EPA should ensure the cleanup money was well spent. The findings target the funding. The report warns that the buried tanks were ticking time bombs. The aquifers could not wait for action.
openalex-w7128725752: A crystal of europium makes odd electricity from magnetism. This lab paper reports a strange sideways voltage in EuTi2Al20, where europium atoms form a diamond-like grid, near its magnetic flip points. The team measured the effect near absolute zero. A study of magnets making their own power.
openalex-w7125686452: Heart failure already limits life; anemia makes it worse. This study of Pakistani patients measured how low red blood cells affect daily functioning in chronic heart failure. The authors quantified the added burden. A clinical study of two burdens compounding.
pmc-13467452: A 2026 review on sirtuins, a family of proteins that help the body respond to calorie restriction, and their role in the pancreas. The authors connect sirtuins to insulin-producing beta cells, metabolism, and aging. For readers following diabetes and longevity research, it is a useful synthesis of a fast-moving field.
pmc-13455352: A 2026 health policy study finding that Medicare beneficiaries without an assigned primary care doctor face greater social disadvantage than those connected to one. The analysis links being "unattributed" — unattached to a physician — to poverty, housing, and other burdens. It argues that getting vulnerable seniors into primary care is also an equity issue.
pmc-13455452: This 2026 transplant paper surveys how providers and centers actually use hypothermic machine perfusion — keeping donor kidneys chilled and pumping with fluid — in deceased-donor kidney transplantation. Practice varies widely, and the study maps that variation. Understanding real-world adoption is the first step toward standardizing a technique that keeps organs viable longer.
pmc-13454952: In this 2026 cancer biology paper, researchers found that tiny vesicles shed by tumors carry double-stranded RNA into platelets, where it triggers the destruction of messenger RNAs for ribosomal proteins. Platelets are reprogrammed by the tumor at a distance. The discovery reveals a new channel of tumor-to-blood communication and a possible biomarker.
pmc-13457352: This 2026 Alzheimer's study profiled gene activity in a 5XFAD;PS19 mouse model — mice engineered to develop Alzheimer's-like pathology — and found distinctive changes in how brain support cells handle fats. The glial lipid dysregulation and coordinated microglial-oligodendrocyte response point to new angles on the disease. The transcriptomic map helps researchers target the brain's immune cells, not just neurons.
pmc-13443052: A 2026 review of clinically useful assessment tools for screening psychiatric disorders in dermatology clinics. Skin disease and mental health are deeply intertwined, yet dermatologists rarely screen for the latter. The paper evaluates which questionnaires actually work in a busy skin clinic.
pmc-13428452: A 2026 scoping review on preventing heterotopic ossification — abnormal bone growth in soft tissue — around the knee. The condition can freeze joints after trauma or surgery, and the review maps what prevention strategies exist. It is a concise guide to a niche but serious problem.
pmc-13425752: A 2026 natural-products review on actinomycin derivatives — structural diversification and biological activities. Actinomycins are potent antibiotics and anticancer agents with a distinctive chromophore. The review catalogs the chemical variants and what they do.
pmc-13412552: A 2026 breast cancer paper combining meta-analysis with multi-omics profiling to study RGS family remodeling — changes in regulators of G protein signaling — as prognostic biomarkers. The integrated approach links gene, protein, and clinical data. The identified markers could refine who needs aggressive treatment.
pmc-13430652: A 2026 software paper introducing SpatialFlux, an R package for distance gradient analysis in spatial transcriptomics — measuring how gene activity changes with distance from a landmark in tissue. Spatial patterns are the new frontier of gene expression. The package gives biologists a ready tool.
pmc-13523552: A 2026 methods paper on preparing high-performance affinity chromatography columns on-column — building the separation medium inside the column itself. The technique simplifies a fiddly lab process. The paper gives chromatographers a practical protocol.
pmc-13279052: This 2026 education study surveyed student and graduate perceptions of how well they developed the core attitudes in the British Pharmacological Society's undergraduate pharmacology curriculum. Attitudes — not just knowledge — are the curriculum's aim. The perceptions reveal where teaching lands and where it misses.
pmc-13559452: A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis framing COPD exacerbation as a short-term cardiopulmonary risk window. The days after a flare are dangerous for the heart too. The time-stratified analysis quantifies the risk.
pmc-13554152: In this 2026 paper, cumulative microscopy revealed cellular states in fibroblasts from patients with genetic disorders. Watching cells over time exposed disease signatures. The method is the advance.
pmc-13424952: In this 2026 interventional radiology paper, bilateral superselective adrenal artery embolization for primary aldosteronism was evaluated for efficacy and safety. The minimally invasive alternative to surgery showed promise. The comparison is the evidence.
pmc-13554752: This 2026 cardiology paper reported survival and health status outcomes following IVUS-guided stent optimization. Imaging-guided stenting was evaluated. The outcomes support the approach.
pmc-13562552: This 2026 cancer paper showed the transcription factor C/EBPβ promotes hyperglycemia-elicited glycolysis and liver cancer progression. High blood sugar fueled tumors via this factor. The mechanism links diabetes to cancer.
pmc-13530752: This 2026 conference poster found pronator-biased pitchers had decreased flexor-pronator strength in supinated positions — a mechanistic rationale for UCL injury. The strength deficit explained the vulnerability. The poster presents the mechanism.
pmc-13526252: A 2026 study (STROKESTOP III) on population reach and participation in opportunistic versus systematic atrial fibrillation screening. The screening strategies were compared. The reach data inform policy.
pmc-13514452: A 2026 Turkish retrospective study of clinical patterns, complications, and long-term visual outcomes of Fuchs' uveitis syndrome in a tertiary center. The eye inflammation's course was charted. The long-term data guide care.
pmc-13537452: A 2026 emergency medicine paper identifying clinical subtypes in acute dyspnea patients via model-based clustering of a prospective cohort. The breathless patients fell into groups. The subtypes guide triage.
pmc-13490752: In this 2026 neuroscience paper, creativity was framed as a white matter connectivity issue — "a (white) matter of connectivity." The brain's wiring underpinned creative thought. The framing is the thesis.
pmc-13461252: This 2026 paper reported procedure-specific morbidity and pathologic assessment after resection of small (≤20 mm) pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. The small tumors' surgery was evaluated. The assessment guides management.
pmc-13454552: In this 2026 paper, bacterial volatile organic compounds mediated a cooperative relationship between bacteria and plants under heavy metal stress. The airborne chemicals brokered the partnership. The mediation is the mechanism.
pmc-13449952: In this 2026 chemistry paper, green ammonia was generated with a polypyridine cobalt complex and visible light. The solar ammonia synthesis is the advance. The complex is the catalyst.
pmc-13575152: A 2026 construction paper optimizing risk management through BIM integration and strategic planning. The building information modeling served risk. The optimizing is the management advance.
pmc-13464952: This 2026 nationwide population-based cohort study linked body roundness index to incident colorectal cancer risk. The body shape metric predicted cancer. The link is the screening signal.
pmc-13429252: This 2026 study found loneliness moderated the association between neighborhood disadvantage and cognitive function among older adults. The loneliness amplified the neighborhood's cognitive toll. The moderating is the insight.
pmc-13427752: A 2026 cognitive science paper: common thought patterns reflected generosity, fairness, and social context. The shared thinking was mapped. The reflecting is the insight.
pmc-13430952: A 2026 paper predicting care needs in community-dwelling older adults using explainable machine learning and a multidimensional approach integrating health, social, and other domains (the title is truncated). The AI forecasted the needs. The predicting is the planning tool.
pmc-13488352: In this 2026 Maine study, seasonality of Vibrio parahaemolyticus in Eastern oysters was tracked along the coast. The pathogen's seasons were mapped. The seasonality informs food safety.
pmc-13560652: In this 2026 paper, bacteriophage Luminis was isolated and genomically characterized — a lytic Yuavirus infecting clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains. The phage's genome was decoded. The characterization serves phage therapy.
pmc-13489152: In this 2026 case report, an entrapped balloon was successfully retrieved during balloon pericardiotomy after rupturing. The surgical rescue was detailed. The retrieval is the feat.
pmc-13467352: In this 2026 pharmacovigilance paper, digoxin dosing errors, drug interactions, and off-label risks were examined via EudraVigilance disproportionality analysis. The old drug's modern risks were quantified. The insights are the safety signal.
pmc-13436552: A 2026 Chinese Han case-control study with sex-stratified analysis of ABCA1 and LIPG polymorphisms' association with coronary heart disease. The lipid genes' heart link was tested. The association is the genetic finding.
pmc-13432852: In this 2026 paper, the TroFuse-011 study design was presented — sacituzumab tirumotecan with or without pembrolizumab for advanced triple-negative breast cancer with PD-L1 CPS <10. The trial design is the contribution. The study will test the combo.
arxiv-2606-16052: Online scams follow repeatable scripts, and catching them takes more than spotting keywords. This paper analyzes scam scenarios at large scale and builds a detection system that follows the whole conversation, not just single messages. The authors map how scam chats unfold and show how a conversation-aware approach can flag fraud more accurately.
arxiv-2606-16152: You would think training a small AI on the best-rated math examples would help it most. This paper finds the opposite: high-reward data can actually impair small models' mathematical reasoning. The authors name it the quality-utility paradox and investigate why it happens, with lessons for anyone training efficient small models on math.
